corpus_row.citation: Lingner J, Hughes TR, Shevchenko A, Mann M, Lundblad V, Cech TR (1997) Reverse transcriptase motifs in the catalytic subunit of telomerase. Science 276(5312):561-567. Claim supported: p123 is the catalytic subunit of Euplotes telomerase and contains bona fide reverse-transcriptase sequence motifs; the paper's entire point is that a host telomere-maintenance enzyme looks like an RT.
corpus_row.expected_class: not a TE - host telomerase reverse transcriptase catalytic subunit (p123/TERT)
corpus_row.why_safe: Confusion axis: this is the landmark record establishing that a host enzyme carries RT motifs 1, 2 and A-E - the single most predictable false positive for an RT-domain TE classifier. Tool-independence: p123 was identified by biochemical purification of the Euplotes telomerase holoenzyme followed by mass-spectrometric peptide sequencing and reverse genetics in yeast (EST2), i.e. protein-level evidence entirely independent of any annotation pipeline. Discrete macronuclear gene deposit (CDS 101..3196), no terminal repeats, no TSDs, not multicopy. Uses ciliate genetic code (transl_table=10).
